Description: Trust in AI scoring: decide how educators can check and, if needed, adjust AI-generated scores. Options: educator override of a criterion rating (with reason), a 'flag for review' option, and a sample-based check of agreement between AI and educator scores. Universities are likely to ask how reliable the AI scoring is; agreement data also supports evidence and validation.

Dashboards: use the AI Coach reflection as learning data. Idea: the learner rates their own performance in the AI Coach reflection (e.g. per competency or on key criteria), and the dashboard compares this self-assessment with the assessed score. This shows whether learners judge their own performance accurately, which is a recognised marker of clinical maturity. To decide: do we want this, what exactly does the learner rate, and how is it shown to learner and educator?

Dashboards: measure transfer of skills to new cases in a fair way. Raw scores across different cases are not comparable because cases differ in difficulty.
